points.text: Claims of consistently outperforming all baselines contradicted by RES, FLU, COV scores
Abstract says 17 LLMs, Section 4.1 says 18 baselines
34,250 sessions includes 20,550 preference pairs, not sessions
Table 3 complete-model scores do not match Table 2 EduDial-LLM row
Training principles mirror evaluation dimensions; baselines may lack scaffold and profiles
GPT-4o filters training data and is the primary evaluator
Test students simulated by models trained on same distribution, favouring EduDial-LLM
No evaluation with real students or teachers and no learning gain
Only 36 scenarios; no CIs, seeds or significance tests despite 'significantly'
Correlation of 0.90 over 18 model means tests ranking, not per-dialogue agreement
Large machine-human gaps on some dimensions, yet machine ratings adopted
No inter-annotator agreement, expert qualifications, blinding or rubric anchors
Number of experts, items reviewed, rejection rate and regeneration cycles not given
No strategy distribution, diversity analysis or math error rate for o1 content
No check that simulated struggling students resemble real students
Grid search and checkpoint selection on the test set
Dated base model; no base or stronger model prompted with scaffold; no generic SFT baseline
Chosen responses from stronger LLM with strategy; length/style bias uncontrolled
Equations 3-5 omit reference model and beta
Test split small and requires specific simulator and GPT-4o judge
Only K-12 math, unstated language; no cross-subject or cross-lingual tests
Drops on Math500 and AIME24 dismissed; teacher statement correctness not measured
Socratic/Bloom tutoring data exists; claims about prior datasets untested
Related work lacks quantitative comparison with prior dialogue datasets
MT-Bench citation appears to be MT-Bench-101; AlpacaEval not multi-turn
Typos and truncated Section 3.5
The 11 dimensions overlap and distinctness is not validated
Data and code not available for assessment
Unclear whether scores from 1v3 or 1v1 setting; Table 2/3 differences unexplained
Teacher may interact with same student model it trained with, reflecting familiarity
Student profiles identically distributed in train and test; OOD performance unknown
Split into 1v3 and 1v1 stages not justified
Differentiated instruction absent from SFT data without rationale
1024-token maximum may be insufficient for long dialogues
Datasets inconsistent between one-on-one and classroom settings; tailoring unclear
Quality of student agent simulation not evaluated
No information on evaluators' qualifications
Similarity of human and machine evaluation cannot rule out expert bias
How the work addresses the cognitive-flow challenge is unclear
SFT+DPO validation cannot separate dataset quality from model training
Base model used for EduDial training not identified
No real-teacher/student data calibration to show classroom logic is reflected
